correctness.rationale: Weighted directed matrix-tree expansion gives each signed character as det L(s), with one signed outgoing arc per nonroot vertex. For odd n the number of trees n^(n-2) is odd, hence every coefficient odd; the constructed (n-1)-order unimodular skew sign matrix with row sums ±1 and root signs cancelling them has det 1. For even n the order n-1 is odd, and L(s) has all odd entries, so row subtraction forces 2^(n-2)|det L(s). The cyclic skew tournament matrix with all root weights +1 produces det(I-A)=2^(n-2), by product of (1-z^h)/(1-z) on the nontrivial odd roots (m=2h+1), while k=(n-2)/2 flipped root arcs yield det(D-J)=0 for n≥4. n=2 is nonsingular. Fourier diagonalization yields the stated Moore-Penrose norm. Independent integer determinant evaluation of both extremizers n=2..11 matched 1/2^(n-2) and even-order zero-star. Finite trials only corroborate the all-order determinant and root-product arguments.
residual_risks: Only bounded checks were independently calculated; infinite assertions rely on actual all-order proof inspection.
